sentences.text: The age of the victim is stated to be 13 years.
Somehow, the victim could save herself from the clutches of the applicant and the co-accused persons and reached her house, as such, the FIR was instituted the same night at about 2.49 am.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF THE APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
It is a clear cut case of false implication.

6. The victim is the consenting party, as is but evident from the CCTV footage taken by the Investigating Officer, as the applicant and the victim are seen going on a motorcycle on 18:59:38 hours on the date of the incident.
Subsequently, on 19:44:41 hours, the applicant was seen going towards the village on motorcycle alone.

In the said CCTV footage, between 19:49:11 hours to 19:49:55 hours, the applicant was seen alongwith one Dheeraj Kumar, going towards the place of occurrence and had on the way beseated the victim on his motorcycle.
The victim was seen seated between the two co-accused persons.
7. The victim being seen going with the applicant twice, implies her consent, as there is no sign of any alarm being raised by her.
8. The age of the victim has deliberately been suppressed.

As per the ossification test report, the age of the victim has come up to be 16 years, as such, a leverage of two years may be granted to the applicant on the upper side.
9.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
10. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 18.9.2023.

The fundamental rights of the applicant as enshrined in Article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated, as only one prosecution witness has been examined i.e. the informant and he has categorically stated that the FIR was not instituted by him.
Rather, it was his daughter, who had instituted the FIR, as such, the prosecution story fails miserably.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/STATE:
11. sentences.text:
CONCLUSION:
12. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.
13.

A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
14.

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
15. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
16. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

17. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the CCTV footage of the victim, the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

18. Let the applicant- Kushal Nishad involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
